A band behind your knees anchored in front, sit back with upright shins. Often used for sore knees.
A brisk walk. Log the minutes.
A burpee onto two dumbbells, then swing them from the floor to overhead in one go.
A chin-up with extra weight on a belt. Log only the added weight.
A deadlift from pins at knee height. Heavy work for the upper back and lockout.
A dip with extra weight on a belt. Log only the added weight. Build up slowly; deep dips stress the shoulder.
A front squat straight into an overhead press in one movement.
A full squat on one leg with the other leg straight out in front.
A heavy one-handed row for high reps with a little body English. Good for grip too.
A hike on hills or trails. Log the minutes.
A hip thrust with most of the weight on the front foot and the back foot only for balance.
A mix of a close-grip press and a skull crusher: lower the bar toward your chin with the elbows forward.
A pull-up that turns into a dip above the bar. Needs strong strict pull-ups and dips first.
A pull-up with extra weight on a belt. Log only the added weight.
A ride outside. Log the minutes; put distance in the note.
A run outside. Log the minutes; put distance in the note.
A small dip and drive with the legs launches the bar, then press it out overhead.
A squat with a two-second pause in the bottom.
An upright row to elbow height, rotate the forearms up, then press. Light only.
Ankle strap on, kick one leg straight back without arching your lower back.
Any ab routine, logged as minutes. Enter how long it took, for example 8.
Arms move in an arc from overhead to your hips. Works the lats without the biceps taking over.
Arms nearly straight, push the bar or rope from eye level down to your thighs. Same movement as the rope pull-over.
Arms open wide in an arc with a soft bend in the elbows. Stop when you feel a stretch, not at the floor.
Arms out in front, roll the weight up and down on the cord.
Arms out to the sides at shoulder height, curl the handles toward your head.
Arms straight in front, pull the band apart to your chest.
Back against a wall, feet out in front, lift your toes as high as you can.
Back against a wall, thighs parallel to the floor. Count seconds.
Back against the pad, feet forward on the platform. Squat deep with your heels down.
Back foot on a bench, lower the back knee toward the floor. Start light.
Balls of the feet on a step under the Smith bar, full stretch and pause at the top.
Band around the knees or ankles, slight squat, step sideways without letting the knees cave.
Bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high, sit straight down.
Bar on your back, hinge forward with a flat back, stand up. Start light.
Bar on your back, step forward into a lunge and push back.
Bar on your upper back, brace, sit down between your hips to at least parallel.
Bar over the middle of your feet, flat back, push the floor away and stand up tall. Reset every rep.
Bell resting on the back of the forearm, press it overhead and lock out.
Bench press from the floor in a rack. Pause when the elbows touch down.
Bench press on a fixed bar path. Set the safety stops just under your chest.
Bench set to about 30 degrees, bar to the upper chest. Shoulder blades pulled back the whole set.
Bent forward at the hips on the machine, rise onto your toes. Big stretch at the bottom.
Body upright on the dip bars, elbows back, lower to about 90 degrees.
Both arms on the pad, curl the handles on a fixed path.
Brisk walking on a steep incline. Easy on the joints, good conditioning.
Cables at shoulder height, step forward and hug the handles together in front of your chest.
Cables crossed at shoulder height, pull them apart with straight arms.
Cables set low, hands sweep up and together to chin height. Keep the range short on the way back.
Chest against the pad, pull the handles to your ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Chest on the pad, row the handles up. Spares the lower back compared with the free T-bar row.
Chest-supported row loaded with plates. Each arm works on its own.
Clean the bar to your shoulders, then drive it overhead with a split of the feet.
Clean the weight to your shoulders, then press it overhead.
Climb the moving stairs without leaning on the rails.
Constant tension from the bottom to the top.
Crunch on a weighted ab machine.
Curl up palms up, turn the palms down at the top, lower slowly.
Cycling on a stationary bike. Log the minutes.
Drop to the floor, push-up optional, jump the feet in and jump up.
Dumbbells on your chest, elbows out, lower the bells toward each other and press back.
Elbow at your side and bent to 90 degrees, rotate the forearm in and out. Very light.
Elbow to the opposite knee, alternating, while the other leg straightens.
Elbows at your sides, curl the bar up without swinging.
Elbows on the pad, extend the arms against the handles.
Elbows pinned at your sides, push down and spread the rope at the bottom.
Face away from a low cable, arm behind you, and curl forward. Big stretch for the long head.
Face away from the stack with the rope behind your head and extend the arms forward and up. Best for the long head.
Face away from the stack, hinge back, then drive the hips forward.
Face down, move through Y, T and W shapes with very light weights. Shoulder health work.
Feet anchored, sit all the way up and lower under control.
Feet locked in, lower the bar to the bottom of your chest. Usually lets you handle a little more than the flat bench.
Feet on a bench, hands on the floor. Harder than a normal push-up and more upper chest.
Feet shoulder width on the platform, lower until your knees are about 90 degrees without lifting your hips.
Forearms on the floor, straight line from head to heels. Count seconds, not reps.
Forearms on the pads, back against the rest, raise your knees.
Forearms on your thighs, palms up, curl the weight with the wrists only.
From a dead hang, pull your shoulder blades down without bending the elbows. Builds the start of every pull-up.
From a hang, bring your toes up to touch the bar.
From the floor to overhead in one explosive pull with one arm.
From your knees, roll forward as far as you can without the lower back sagging.
Full stretch at the bottom, pause, then rise onto your toes.
Go from lying down to standing with a kettlebell held overhead, step by step, and back down.
Guided overhead press. An option when free weights bother the shoulder.
Guided press at an upward angle. Set the seat so the handles start at upper chest height.
Hammer curl across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Hammer curl with a rope on a low cable, constant tension.
Hammer-style chest press loaded with plates. Log the plates on one side or the total, but always the same way.
Hands about shoulder width, elbows close to your body, bar to the lower chest.
Hands on a bench behind you, lower your hips. Hard on the front of the shoulder.
Hands on a bench, body straight. The higher the hands, the easier it gets.
Hands on handles or plates so your chest goes below hand level for a longer stretch.
Hands together under your chest with thumbs and index fingers in a diamond.
Hands under your shoulders, elbows brushing your sides.
Hands well outside shoulder width. Harder than a normal pull-up.
Hang from a bar and raise straight legs to hip height or higher.
Hang from a bar and raise your knees toward your chest without swinging.
Hang from a bar with relaxed shoulders. Count seconds.
Hang under a bar set at waist height, body straight, pull your chest to the bar. Walk the feet back to make it harder.
Heels on a plate or wedge so the knees travel forward and the quads work harder.
Hinge and snap the hips forward to swing the bell to chest height. A hip movement, not a squat or an arm raise.
Hinge at the hips on the bench and lift until your body is in a straight line. Do not arch past neutral.
Hinge at the hips with almost straight legs until the hamstrings stretch, then stand up.
Hinge forward with a dumbbell in each hand and row both to your hips.
Hinge forward with a flat back and row the weight to your chest. End the set when your back starts to round.
Hinge forward, upper arm along your side, extend the arm back behind you.
Hinge forward, upper arm still, straighten the elbow until the arm points back.
Hinge on one leg while the other reaches back. Keep the hips square.
Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back and row the bar to your lower ribs.
Hips high in an upside-down V, lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Hold a plate straight out in front and turn it left and right like a steering wheel.
Hold a post and lean away, raise one dumbbell out to the side. Harder at the bottom than the normal raise.
Hold one dumbbell behind your head with both hands and extend the arms up.
Hold one dumbbell flat on your palms like a tray and curl it.
Hold one weight at your chest and squat deep. Good for learning the movement.
Hold the bench behind your head and lower your straight body like a lever.
Hold the end of a landmine bar at your chest and squat. Good for learning depth.
Hold the end of the bar overhead with straight arms and swing it side to side in an arc.
Hold yourself up on straight arms with the legs straight out in front.
In a push-up position on dumbbells, row one up at a time without twisting the hips.
In a push-up position, drive the knees toward your chest one after the other.
In a push-up position, tap each shoulder with the opposite hand without the hips rocking.
Incline press on the Smith machine. Place the bench so the bar touches your upper chest.
Incline version of the plate-loaded press. Each arm moves on its own, so weak sides show.
Jump onto a box and land quietly. Step down, do not jump down.
Kick up against a wall and lower your head to the floor. Start with pike push-ups.
Kickback on a guided machine with a chest pad.
Kneel facing the stack and crunch your ribs toward your hips.
Kneel or stand on the platform and pull up. Log the assistance; lower is better.
Kneel with heels anchored and lower your body forward as slowly as you can. Catch yourself with your hands.
Kneeling upright, lean back slowly with a straight line from knees to head, then come back.
Knees bent, this works the deeper calf muscle.
Laps in the pool. Log the minutes; put distance or strokes in the note.
Lean back and let the knees travel far forward. Hold on to something.
Lean forward a little and lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Lean into the handles and drive the sled with short powerful steps.
Leg curl one leg at a time, standing.
Leg extension one leg at a time.
Legs nearly straight, lower the weight toward the floor with a flat back.
Lie back on an incline bench so the arms hang behind your body. The stretch loads the long head, and can bother the front of the shoulder.
Lie chest-down on an incline with the arms hanging straight and curl.
Lie face down and curl the pad toward your glutes.
Lie face down and lift arms and legs off the floor. Hold, breathe, lower.
Lie face down on a raised bench and row from a dead hang. No cheating possible.
Lie face down on an incline and raise light dumbbells into a Y shape.
Lie face down on an incline bench and row the dumbbells up. No lower back stress.
Lie face down over the end of a bench and swing the legs up to a straight line.
Lie on a bench and lower the weight toward your forehead by bending only the elbows.
Lie on your back with your feet toward the stack and curl a bar from a low cable.
Lie on your side, elbow on your hip and bent 90 degrees, rotate the forearm up. Very light.
Lift the ball overhead and slam it into the floor as hard as you can.
Lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, lower. No rolling.
Long stance, both feet on the floor, drop the back knee straight down.
Low cable behind you, raise the handle to shoulder height in front.
Low-impact cardio on the elliptical. Log the minutes.
Lower back on the ball, crunch up. The ball lets you stretch back first.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor. Lean forward a little to bring in the chest.
Lying across or along a bench, lower one dumbbell behind your head with almost straight arms and pull it back over.
Lying flat, lift arms and legs together and touch your toes at the top.
Lying on the floor with the bar over your hips, drive them up and squeeze.
Lying on your side with knees bent, open the top knee like a shell.
Lying with legs straight up, lower them side to side under control.
Machine squat on a swinging arc. Very deep knee bend with back support.
Machine-guided curl, one arm at a time, on a fixed path.
Make waves with both ropes for a set time. Logged in minutes.
On hands and feet with knees just off the floor, crawl forward with a flat back.
On hands and knees, lift one bent leg out to the side.
On hands and knees, press one foot up toward the ceiling with the knee bent.
On hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg out long and hold a second.
On one forearm with your body in a straight line. Count seconds.
On the glute-ham bench, lower forward and curl back up using the hamstrings.
On your back with heels on a ball, lift the hips and roll the ball in.
On your back with the soles of the feet together, knees out, and pump the hips up.
On your back, curl your hips off the floor toward your chest.
On your back, curl your ribs toward your hips. Small range, no pulling on the neck.
On your back, knees bent, push your hips up until your body is straight.
On your back, legs just off the floor, kick small and fast.
On your back, lower back pressed down, arms and legs held just off the floor.
On your back, lower straight legs toward the floor while your lower back stays down.
On your back, lower the opposite arm and leg while your lower back stays flat.
One arm at a time across your body. Easier to feel the chest work and to fix a weaker side.
One arm over the preacher pad, curl through the full range.
One dumbbell behind your head, elbow pointing up, extend.
One foot in the middle of the platform. Shows the difference between your legs.
One foot on a step, dumbbell in the same hand, rise up and lower slowly.
One foot on a step, hold something for balance, full range.
One hand and one knee on a bench, row the dumbbell toward your hip.
One handle, pull your elbow down to your side. Fixes a side that lags.
Open the arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Overhead press sitting on the floor with straight legs. No leg drive, no leaning back.
Pads on the outside of your arms, raise them to shoulder height.
Palms face each other all the way. Builds the muscle under the biceps and the forearms.
Palms facing each other. The easiest grip on the shoulders and elbows.
Palms facing you, shoulder width. A bit easier on the lats than a pull-up and harder on the biceps.
Pinch two plates together smooth sides out and hold.
Press lying on the floor. The floor stops the elbows early, which spares the shoulders.
Press the end of a landmine bar up and forward with one hand. Kind to sore shoulders.
Press the platform with your toes only, with a full stretch at the bottom.
Press two dumbbells from a slight decline. Have a spotter hand them to you or kick them up carefully.
Press two dumbbells overhead from shoulder height.
Press two dumbbells up from a bench set to about 30 degrees. Lower until your upper arms are about level with the bench.
Press two dumbbells up from chest level. Keep the elbows at about 45 degrees from your torso.
Press two dumbbells while squeezing them together the whole time.
Pull a close neutral handle to your upper chest. A longer range than the wide bar.
Pull the bar from the floor explosively and catch it on your shoulders in a quarter squat. Learn it light.
Pull the bar from the floor to overhead in one movement with a wide grip. Very technical.
Pull the bar to your upper chest while leaning back slightly. Drive the elbows down, not the hands.
Pull the elbows back as you curl so the bar slides up along your body.
Pull the handle diagonally across your body from high to low, turning from the hips.
Pull the handles down and back from above, like a pulldown and a row combined.
Pull the handles down from overhead while hinging at the hips, like double-poling.
Pull the opposite cable across in front of your face and extend the arm out to the side.
Pull the rope toward your face with the elbows high and wide, then rotate the hands up. Light weight.
Pulls the weight up to your chest with the elbows high. It often irritates the shoulder joint.
Push with the legs first, then lean back and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Push-up from the knees with a straight line from head to knees. The first step toward full push-ups.
Pushdown with an angled bar. Often the heaviest pushdown handle.
Pushdown with palms up. Lighter weight, strict elbows.
Raise a plate held at both sides to eye level.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides up to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise the weight in front of you to shoulder height. Most people already get plenty of front delt work from presses.
Reverse hyper machine or high bench
Rounds on a heavy bag. Log the total minutes.
Row a rope to your face with the elbows high and out to the sides.
Row a wide bar to your lower chest with the elbows flared. More upper back than lats.
Running on a treadmill. Log the minutes; put pace or distance in the note.
Seated or kneeling, row one handle to your hip and let the shoulder reach forward on the way back.
Seated or lying bridge on a machine with a hip pad.
Seated press on a fixed bar path in front of your face.
Seated press on a guided path. Easy to control and easy to stop when the shoulder complains.
Seated row on a machine with a chest pad. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.
Seated upright so you cannot swing. Turn the palms up as you curl.
Seated version of the leg curl. It stretches the hamstrings more at the start.
Seated, elbow braced against the inside of your thigh, curl slowly.
Seated, lower the bar behind your head and press it back up.
Seated, pads on the inside of the knees. Squeeze the legs together, pause, and let them open slowly.
Seated, pads on the outside of the knees. Press the legs apart, pause, and bring them back slowly. Keep your torso still.
Seated, push the handles down. A controlled version of the dip.
Seven reps on the bottom half, seven on the top half, seven full. Light weight.
Shoulders under the pads, squat on the angled sled.
Shrug on a machine. Lift straight up toward the ears and pause.
Side plank with the top leg on a bench and the bottom leg off the floor.
Sit leaning back with feet up and rotate side to side.
Sit tall, pull the handle to your belly with the shoulder blades back. No rocking.
Small quick bounces on the balls of your feet with stiff ankles.
Small quick jumps on the balls of the feet. Log the minutes.
Squat back to a box, pause without relaxing, stand up.
Squat down and jump as high as you can, land softly.
Squat holding a medicine ball, stand and throw it to a target on the wall, catch and repeat.
Squat on a fixed bar path. Feet slightly forward.
Squat with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Squeeze one or two plates between your palms at chest height and press them straight out.
Stand between two cables and press the handles forward and slightly together.
Stand between two high cables and bring your hands down and together in front of your hips.
Stand inside the hex bar and stand up with it. Easier to learn than the barbell deadlift.
Stand side-on to a landmine and row the end of the bar with one hand.
Stand side-on to the cable, press the handle straight out and resist the rotation.
Standing side-on to a low cable, lift the outside leg out to the side.
Standing side-on to a low cable, pull the inside leg across in front of the other.
Standing tall, bend sideways toward the dumbbell and come back up.
Standing, curl one arm at a time without swinging.
Standing, squeeze the glutes and press the bar overhead, moving your head back out of the way and through.
Start from a full hang and pull your chest toward the bar. Lower under control.
Start with palms facing you, rotate them forward as you press up.
Step backward into the lunge. Easier on the knees than stepping forward.
Step forward into a lunge and alternate legs.
Step onto a bench and stand up fully, then lower under control.
Step wide to one side and sit into that hip with the other leg straight.
Straddle the bar and row the end with a close grip handle to your chest.
Straight line from head to heels, lower your chest to the floor. Put your hands on a bench to make it easier.
Straighten the knees against the pad and lower slowly.
Swing the bell up so it lands softly in the rack position at your shoulder.
The arms sweep together in an arc. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and do not let the handles go behind your torso.
The assisted machine with palms facing you. Log the assistance; lower is better.
The back extension holding a plate at your chest. Stop at a straight line.
The barbell curl on an angled bar, easier on the wrists.
The bell between your feet, hinge down and stand up. The first step toward swings.
The clean started from just above the knees.
The fan bike that pushes back harder the faster you go. Good for intervals.
The fly on a 30 degree bench. Light weight, slow stretch at the bottom.
The glute bridge on one foot with the other knee pulled in.
The load hangs from a hip belt, so your back carries nothing.
The main heavy press. Feet planted, shoulder blades pulled back, bar to the lower chest.
The overhead press seated with back support. Lower to chin height.
The padded bar with handles in front. Easy on stiff shoulders.
The same movement with a straight bar. You can usually use a little more weight than with the rope.
The same raise as with dumbbells, but the cable keeps tension on at the bottom.
The sit-up on a decline bench. Hold a plate to make it harder.
The wrist curl with palms down. Use less weight.
Torso parallel to the floor, each rep starts from the floor. Explosive pull, controlled lower.
Two kettlebells on the floor, wide stance, row them one at a time while the other stays down.
Two low cables crossed, raise the handles up and out into a Y.
Underhand grip, torso more upright than a barbell row. Pull the bar to your belly.
Upper arms resting on the pad, curl through the full range.
Upper back on a bench, drive the hips up until your body is flat and squeeze the glutes.
Upper back on a bench, drive up through one foot.
Very wide stance, hands inside the knees, push the knees out and stand up.
Very wide stance, toes out, hold one weight between your legs and squat.
Walk with a heavy weight in each hand, tall posture, short steps.
Walk with a weight in one hand without leaning toward it.
Walking with a loaded backpack. Note the weight you carried.
Wide hands, shift your weight over one arm while the other stays almost straight.
Wide stance, shift down onto one leg until the other leg is straight with toes up.
